results.reason: The memo identifies §2.2's automatic five-year renewal and the 270/240-day notice window. It calculates the window as October 3 to November 2, 2026, explains lock-in through June 30, 2032 with escalating commitments, and recommends serving protective notice or getting a signed amendment before November 2.

The memo identifies the §5.3 30-day objection right and deemed acceptance. It notes the 14% increase effective November 1, 2026 and receipt on August 21, giving a September 20 deadline. It concludes the right has almost certainly lapsed, recommends confirming with the client whether an objection was sent, and otherwise recommends negotiating a concession.

The memo explains that §11.1 is broad enough to cover Brightmere-caused claims such as design defects and failure to warn, that §12.3(a) puts it outside the cap, and that Brightmere's §11.2 indemnity remains capped. It recommends narrowing §11.1 to Halvorsen's fault and making the exclusion mutual or capping Halvorsen's indemnity.

The memo identifies that First Amendment §3 deletes and replaces §12.3 and drops the recall carve-out. It explains that recall reimbursement is now subject to the 12-month cap, which a large recall could exceed, and recommends reinstating the carve-out.

The memo identifies that First Amendment §6 selects Delaware law and exclusive Wilmington jurisdiction, notes the conflict with DA §§17.1–17.2, and says the amendment prevails under §1.4. It recommends conforming governing law and forum back to New York.
The memo states that receipt occurred on August 21, 2026.
The memo states that the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
The memo states that under Section 1.4 written amendments take precedence over the Agreement body.
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each issue has 'Where', 'Why it matters for Halvorsen', and 'Recommended fix' sections.
The memo expressly states that recall reimbursement can no longer be treated as outside the cap.
The memo acknowledges the Delaware provisions and concludes that Delaware law and forum now presumptively apply.
